reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes a PancakeSwap sniper bot with a specific high daily earnings claim and directs viewers to a free trial and paid license. It demonstrates connecting the bot to MetaMask for automated token trading and ties the claimed financial benefit to purchasing and using the product. the available video evidence does not establish actual profits, losses, transaction details, or whether the advertised returns are typical or guaranteed.

citations.quote: +2500$ PER DAY / Pancakeswap Bot / Best Pancakeswap Sniper Bot Free / BSC Sniper Bot / Trust Wallet
This bot works with 10 wallets at the same time which in the long run can bring you great money if you have the resources to do so.
In this video I will show you how to set up and how to connect the bot to MetaMask.
This bot will automatically buy and sell your chosen token.
Automatically Buy/Sell Trade Functions

opening.argument: The material presents automated trading as conditional and user-configured, not as a guaranteed income scheme. The spoken claim says that multiple wallets can bring money only “if you have the resources to do so,” which expressly limits the claim rather than promising results. The interface also exposes operational risk controls, including buy and sell settings, slippage, and stop-loss fields, while the description identifies automatically configured “take profit and stop-loss” features. Those details are consistent with a tool whose results depend on settings, resources, and market conditions. A headline figure alone does not establish that the presenter guarantees that outcome to every viewer.

citations.quote: This bot works with 10 wallets at the same time which in the long run can bring you great money if you have the resources to do so.
Take profit and stop-loss are set automatically

rebuttal.rebuttal: The title’s dollar figure is attention-grabbing, but the prosecution does not show that it is stated as a guaranteed or typical return. Its other quotations establish automation and setup, not deception. The spoken qualification makes financial benefit conditional on having sufficient resources, and the displayed controls show that trading parameters and loss protection are part of the configuration. The evidence therefore supports a conditional tool demonstration, not a promise that viewers will receive the advertised amount.

citations.quote: +2500$ PER DAY / Pancakeswap Bot / Best Pancakeswap Sniper Bot Free / BSC Sniper Bot / Trust Wallet
With the setting of what price to buy and sell, I think you'll figure it out on your own.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The qualification about resources does not withdraw the earnings implication: it says the bot can bring “great money,” while the title supplies a specific daily amount. Stop-loss and take-profit controls describe trading features, not evidence that the advertised returns are realistic. The material still directs viewers toward the product and its use, and nothing cited verifies profits, representative performance, or the basis for the headline figure.

+2500$ PER DAY / Pancakeswap Bot / Best Pancakeswap Sniper Bot Free / BSC Sniper Bot / Trust Wallet

opening.argument: The presentation is most naturally read as an operational demonstration and tutorial. The speaker explicitly says, “In this video I will show you how to set up and how to connect the bot to MetaMask,” then describes automated buying and selling and leaves the price settings for the viewer to determine. The sampled screens show a configurable bot interface beside token information, with token addresses, buy and sell fields, timing, slippage, and start/stop controls. That is instructional material about operating software: it shows how the tool is configured and run, without supplied evidence of a completed profitable trade or a promised outcome.

citations.quote: In this video I will show you how to set up and how to connect the bot to MetaMask.
With the setting of what price to buy and sell, I think you'll figure it out on your own.

rebuttal.rebuttal: Calling the material a tutorial does not make it a scam. The prosecution identifies a product and a trading workflow, but those are precisely the subject matter of an operational demonstration. The visible sequence shows configuration and status output rather than a claimed profit result, and the cited speech explains setup rather than instructing viewers to transfer funds to the presenter. The evidence supports technology education with promotional context, not certification of an earnings claim.

citations.quote: In this video I will show you how to set up and how to connect the bot to MetaMask.

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The tutorial framing does not remove the commercial message. The title advertises “+2500$ PER DAY,” the description offers a free trial and a license, and the narration says the bot can bring “great money.” Showing setup and automation is how the product’s proposed financial use is demonstrated; it does not establish that the earnings claim is educationally neutral or supported by actual results.

TRY NOW 30-DAYS FREE TRIAL
This bot will automatically buy and sell your chosen token.

opening.argument: This is ordinary software promotion for a trading utility, and the supplied material does not show the mechanisms that would make it a conventional scam. The description offers a time-limited trial and separately says, “Buy a license,” which is a recognizable product-access model. The interface shows configurable trading inputs and a start/stop workflow, while the description lists supported systems and bot features. No supplied source shows a deposit to the presenter, a request for credentials, a downline, or a guaranteed payout. A product may be promoted without the record proving that its external service is unsafe or that its marketing figure is guaranteed.

The bot working with Windows/Linux/MAC

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution’s evidence identifies a promoted bot, but promotion and an advertised price do not by themselves establish a scam mechanism. The description presents software access, a trial period, and a license, while the frames show the tool operating with user-entered parameters. The record does not show the presenter taking a deposit, collecting a wallet secret, promising a payout, or recruiting participants. It therefore supports an ordinary commercial referral or software demonstration, with the product’s safety left unverified rather than disproved.

citations.quote: 30-day free period of use, from the moment you install the bot on your PC
Buy a license

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The absence of a shown deposit or credential request does not answer the central issue. The content pairs a specific daily earnings headline with a bot that automatically buys and sells tokens, then directs viewers to a free trial and paid license. A conventional scam need not display every harmful step in the sampled frames. The commercial format and missing evidence of actual or typical profits leave the earnings-oriented promotion unsupported.
